articles.title: JetBlue raises bag fees for third time in a year as fuel costs bite
articles.summary: JetBlue Airways has raised the price of checking a bag for many customers for the third time in less than a year as high fuel costs continue to eat into the industry's profits. Checking a first bag for travelers booked in economy will now be $50, up from $45, if purchased more than 24 hours before departure during a non-peak travel period. If it's paid within 24 hours of departure, the fee will be $60.

articles.title: Options traders are betting heavily on these stocks ahead of election results
articles.summary: With prediction markets pricing in a big victory for Democrats in Tuesday's midterm elections, traders are leaning into a group of stocks that investors often categorize as beneficiaries of left-wing leadership. Options trading in clean-energy stocks, particularly solar companies, surged on Tuesday, despite a five-month sell-off in the group that's left most of the companies in the industry group down on the year.

articles.title: Meta seeks to raise up to $25 billion in debt sale as AI spending jumps
articles.summary: Meta is seeking to raise between $20 billion and $25 billion in a bond sale on Tuesday as the company ramps up its spending on artificial intelligence infrastructure along with AI models and services. Final pricing for the bond sale should come Tuesday afternoon, the sources said. Meta previously raised $25 billion in an April bond sale, and said last week that it plans to raise $95 billion in an effort to fund its AI initiatives.

articles.title: Shopify falls 7% after Q3 revenue and merchandise volume miss estimates
articles.summary: Shares of e-commerce platform Shopify fell 7% on Tuesday after the company missed estimates on subscription gross profit and gross merchandise volume. Shopify said it sees revenue growth in the "low thirties" range year over year for the fourth quarter, versus LSEG estimates of 32.1%.

articles.title: Bill Ackman warns of 'casino' stock market as speculative trading grows
articles.summary: "Every number of days, I feel like markets are broken," Ackman said on CNBC's "Squawk Box." "Stocks trade at prices that make no sense to me. "I don't think that's inherently good for the economy, for society, and it's leading to these massive moves in stocks." The founder of Pershing Square Capital Management said those same dislocations in the market have given the hedge fund the opportunity to snag big bargains.
